# The decoders of LOCAL bytes: compressed streams, filesystem images, image
# formats. Swept NIGHTLY by .github/workflows/vuln.yml, beside
# vulnscan-exposed.txt and vulnscan-tools.txt.
#
# ⛔ THEY WERE `workflow_dispatch` ONLY FOR ONE DAY, AND THAT WAS A MEASUREMENT
# TAKEN IN THE WRONG PLACE -- kept here because the mistake is more useful than
# the number. On 2026-10-31 a 58-repository sweep from the WORKSTATION answered
#
#   58 scanned: CLEAN 44, UNREAD 14   (every failure a `git clone … 403`,
#                                      and a push from the same machine was
#                                      refused minutes later)
#
# so the nightly list was cut to 22 and these 49 were relegated to a dispatch,
# with the argument written out at length. The first real run from a RUNNER, on
# 2026-11-01, answered differently:
#
#   9 exposed  : 9 scanned,  0 UNREAD
#   49 decoders: 49 scanned, 0 UNREAD   (48 seconds)
#   13 tools   : 13 scanned, 0 UNREAD
#   -> 72 clones in one run, nothing unread
#
# The ceiling belonged to that workstation's unauthenticated requests, not to
# the runner that executes the lane. A limit measured from the wrong client is a
# property of the instrument, not of the subject.
#
# ⛔ One run of 72 clones is not proof of a steady state, and that is acceptable
# for one reason: the failure is VISIBLE. UNREAD names the repositories and
# vulnscan exits 2, so a night that does meet the limit says so rather than
# going quiet. `-state` is passed so a person can finish a partial run with
# `-retry-unread`; the in-tool retry is issue #150.
#
# ⛔ AND IT MUST NOT BE CARRIED BETWEEN NIGHTS: a repository that was CLEAN
# yesterday is not clean today if an advisory was published since. The code does
# not change; the DATABASE does, which is the whole reason this runs on a clock.
#
# ⛔ SLICING ACROSS THE WEEK STAYS REJECTED, and that part was never about the
# limit: it keeps everything in view while reintroducing the latency a clock
# exists to remove -- an advisory published on Monday would reach Friday's slice
# on Friday, and the founding case is two advisories found 2 and 4 days late.
#
# Last full pass: 2026-10-31, 58 scanned, 56 clean, 2 reaching GO-2026-6860 --
# both network-facing, both now fixed, and both now in vulnscan-exposed.txt.
